title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page is the continuation (item 5) of a proposition begun on p.41. There V is a 2-dimensional F_2-vector space, Γ = Aut(V) = GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3 acting on the three nonzero vectors, and M = End(V) is the 4-dimensional F_2-algebra of 2×2 matrices. Earlier items: (1) the three transpositions (involutions of GL_2(F_2)), together with 0, form a canonical 2-dimensional subspace V' ⊂ End(V), isomorphic to V as a Γ-module. (2) The three even elements {1, ρ, ρ²}, together with 0, form a 2-dimensional subspace W ≅ F_4 inside End(V). (3) V' and W are orthogonal for the trace form. (4) W is a nonsplit extension 0 → F_2·1 → W → F_2 → 0 via the trace. Item 5 on this page reads: sl(V) := Ker(M --Tr--> F_2) = V' + F_2·1_V. In words, the trace-zero part of End(V) is spanned by the transpositions and the identity. Check: involutions in GL_2(F_2) are unipotent with trace 0. In characteristic 2, Tr(1_V) = 2 = 0. 1_V does not lie in V'. So V' + F_2·1 is 3-dimensional and contained in the 3-dimensional kernel of the trace, hence equal to it. Moreover the sum is direct and Γ-stable, so sl(V) ≅ V ⊕ F_2 as a Γ-module, whereas End(V) itself is not semisimple in this way (the subspace W ≅ F_4 has a nonsplit filtration). The surrounding context is the study of level-2 structures (the 2-torsion E[2] as a rank-2 F_2-module with S_3 symmetry) for the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. The next page starts section II on the structure of the 2-torsion with respect to P^1, i.e. Legendre-type branch points.

ideas.what: Over F_2, the trace-zero part of End(V) (dim V = 2) decomposes as the span of the three involutions of GL_2(F_2) plus the scalars: sl(V) = V' ⊕ F_2·1, Γ-equivariantly. This reflects that sl_2 is not simple in characteristic 2 (the centre contains the scalars).
ideas.modern_name: Structure of sl_2(F_2) / gl_2 in characteristic 2 as an S_3-module

deep.surprise_reason: This is a single-line, correct, elementary linear-algebra remark completing a routine description of End(F_2^2) as an S_3-module, in preparation for level-2 structures on elliptic curves. Nothing here is new.
